title: mUnit glossary
description: The terms shown by Extras > mUnit > mUnit Glossary and rendered into the Glossary section of README.md. The patch reads this file with [dict] when it opens; the README is rendered from it by the build (pnpm run glossary), which also checks that every term points at a help patcher, example, manual heading and term that exists.

categories.description: Shown in this order, as the entries of the category menu and the sub-headings of the README section.

terms.description: Shown in this order. Put the general idea before the mUnit detail.

term.description: The word or phrase, unique across every category. Other terms name it in their "also" lists exactly as written here.

definition.description: One to three sentences of plain prose: what the idea is, then how mUnit does it. Write object names in brackets, [mUnit.assert]; the README renders them as code. No double quotes, which Max would strip.

also.description: Related terms, each the exact "term" of another entry. May be empty.

see.description: Where to go next: the Go to buttons in Max and the See links in the README, in this order. At least one.

label.description: The button text in Max. The README renders the target itself, except for a url, which uses this label.

action.description: What the button does, a verb and a target: "help <object>" opens a help patcher (an object with a docs/<object>.maxref.xml); "load <patch>" opens an example (examples/<patch>/<patch>.maxpat) or an Extras patch by name; "readme <slug>" opens that heading of README.md on GitHub, the slug being the heading in lower case with punctuation removed and spaces as hyphens, as GitHub makes its anchors; "url <https://...>" opens a web page.
